findings.reason: The protected solution is concise, conventional, and interview-ready. The root, target, smaller_right, greater, smaller, and greater_left names expose which partition and child fragment each recursive result represents, with no generic local named index. The app-local TreeNode is minimal, defines only __init__, and carries the required Local equivalent documentation.

When root.val <= target, BST ordering places root and its entire left subtree in the smaller component, so only the right subtree can straddle the threshold. Recursively splitting that child and attaching its smaller fragment back to root.right preserves the smaller BST while returning the greater fragment separately. The symmetric root.val > target branch classifies root and its whole right subtree as greater, splits only the left child, and attaches its greater fragment to root.left. The null base case terminates both boundary paths. Induction along the single threshold search path proves every original node appears exactly once on the correct side, both outputs remain BSTs, and all untouched parent-descendant relationships are preserved.

Metadata consistently identifies Premium LeetCode problem 776, Python, and the native splitBST(root, target) interface. Authenticated source evidence confirms a 1-through-50-node BST, node and target values from 0 through 1000, a threshold that need not occur, values <= target in the first subtree, values > target in the second, preservation of every original parent-child relationship whose nodes remain together, and the ordered two-root return. The app-local adapter preserves that contract.

The protected app recursion and immutable native source bound to verified submission 2066086059 are algorithmically identical: both use the same null base case, branch on root.val <= target, recurse only into the ambiguous child, reconnect the same-side returned fragment, and return smaller then greater roots. The app adds only the required minimal local TreeNode and calls solve recursively where the native wrapper calls Solution.splitBST.

The three authored workloads grow height-balanced BSTs from 3 to the source maximum of 50 nodes and split at the root value, forcing the protected recursion down one logarithmic threshold path while a semantics-preserving full-tree prescan must visit every node before applying the same in-place split. In the final independent run, the exact protected source passed all 11 visible correctness cases and all three performance tiers with relative growth exponent +0.00 and a 1.02x largest runtime ratio. The independently correct node-reusing prescan control matched every output but failed only performance with relative growth exponent +0.29, above the allowed +0.15, distinguishing O(h) path rewiring from O(n) full-tree scanning.

The Approach accurately derives which child alone can straddle the threshold in each branch, why the opposite subtree is already classified by BST ordering, how reconnecting the same-side fragment preserves structure, and why recursion visits only one node per level. Its O(h) time and O(h) call-stack claims match the protected implementation and branch manifest.

The modular Reference preserves the source's three-part contract narrative, exact two-example sequence without invented explanations, two constraints, and single recursive hint. Its accessible Mermaid replacement for the source image reproduces the original Example 1 tree, both returned roots, every node, and every resulting edge.

A fresh authenticated Premium review verified exactly two unexplained examples in source order, two constraints, one hint, one meaningful source image, and no tables, notes, or follow-up. The modular files are hash-bound in source_fidelity.json to source content hash 3906487032141f68f63b42a210b483ba71606431033c23645bffb9096826c77e, and the direct fidelity validator returns verified with no errors.

coverage: The authenticated Premium statement contains exactly two examples. The real singleton example was promoted from a trial to sample-2, while the two invented source-labelled examples were retained only as separately labelled visible trials where useful. Both exact source examples now appear first in source order.

All 11 ordinary correctness cases are visible samples or trials. Contract boundaries cover 1 and 50 nodes, Node.val and target values 0 and 1000, a threshold below every node, a threshold at or above every node, and thresholds both present and absent from the BST.

Material topology covers balanced, left-skewed, and right-skewed trees; root, internal, leaf, and absent thresholds; empty first and second results; deep reconnection on both sides; ordered output roots; strict partitioning at <= target versus > target; and preservation of original same-component parent-child relationships.

An independent iterative two-spine splitter recomputed every authored expected tree. For every protected result, identity-based checks proved that the outputs were disjoint, contained exactly the original node objects with no loss, duplication, or replacement, remained strict BSTs, obeyed the ordered value partition, and retained every original same-component parent-child edge.

The independent oracle, protected app source, and immutable native Solution agreed on all 14 authored correctness-plus-benchmark inputs, 2548 exhaustive BST-shape and threshold pairs through six nodes, 5000 deterministic random legal trees through 50 nodes, and four explicit node-count/value/target boundary inputs; the protected source also passed the complete real-test path.

The repaired 3-, 15-, and 50-node height-balanced workloads remain hidden and performance-only, span more than 16x, and make the independently correct node-reusing O(n) full-tree prescan fail only the scaling verdict against O(h) path rewiring.
